correctness.rationale: The proof applies the primary source's Lemma 39 equivalence K_Cn iff phase choice T(n) for families of directed n-cycles. If n=dr, canonically replace each d-cycle by its product with {0,..,r-1}; its induced n-phase has unique zero whose first coordinate gives a d-origin. For ab-cycles, quotient by s^b-orbits to obtain b-cycle, choose an orbit with T(b), then a root in that a-cycle with T(a). Both constructions are definable in ZF without unmentioned global choice. Prime-factor induction proves K_Cn iff conjunction K_Cp for p|n; Corollary 59 gives missing-prime nonimplications under Con(ZF). For finite choice Theorem 42 plus factorization gives prime basis, though prior introductory Lemma 9 appears already to state this. Limits: no arbitrary digraph classification and no independent consistency proof.
residual_risks: The source introduction Lemma 9 prints a prime-cycle basis, though its index is inconsistent and body Theorem 42 is all cycles; consequently the AC(N) prime-only consequence may already have been claimed. Originality rests narrowly on explicit classification of single composite-cycle principles and implication criterion.
The precise ZF separation direction inherits Corollary 59 and Con(ZF); it is not an unconditional independence proof.
The only templates classified here are single directed cycles.
